newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels and EU assembly do battle over car park.
newsitem.headline: Brussels and EU assembly do battle over car park.

text.p: The European Parliament could soon find itself the owner of a costly white elephant -- a 2,300 place underground car park of which it can use only 900 spaces.

Brussels residents and the city's environment agency, citing a report by the European Commission, want to stop the assembly using most of the car park under its 40 billion Belgian franc ($1.2 billion) headquarters to ease the daily traffic jams in the area.

In a letter to the parliament on Friday Brussels Environment Minister Didier Gosuin cited the results of a study by the Commission, the European Union's executive, which recommended cutting the number of parking spaces available to EU civil servants to ease car traffic in Brussels's European quarter.
He pointed out that the parliament itself had recommended that measures should be taken to limit car use in cities.
Developers Societe Forum Leopold have contested the plan to limit the places in the car park which is due to come into use in April.
Gosuin challenged the parliament to state clearly before the end of March, when it is due to sign a 27-year lease on the building, whether it needs all the places.
"In the absence of a response I propose to consider you approve of the position formalised by our administration (for 900 places)," Gosuin said in his letter.
If the Brussels regional government blocked the developer's appeal, "we would require internal work (in the car parks) to stop their use by vehicles," Gosuin told a news conference.
The extra space would have to be used for storage or be converted into meeting areas, he said.
